name: CS Cha

planets.name: B
planets.note: First imaged by Ginski et al. 2018 (arXiv:1805.02261) as a polarized point source at ~1.3"/220 AU outside the resolved circumbinary disk, initially interpreted as a possible planetary-mass/brown-dwarf companion (~9-35 Mjup) with a circum-companion disk. A dedicated follow-up spectrum (Haffert et al. 2020, A&A 640, L12, arXiv:2007.07831, 'CS Cha B: A disc-obscured M-type star mimicking a polarised planetary companion') found CS Cha B is instead a heavily extincted M-type (very low-mass) star with its own disk, not a planet or brown dwarf. Status set to 'refuted' as a planetary-mass object per current literature; both papers cited for traceability. Distinct from the unrelated new candidate 'CS Cha c' point source reported by Follette et al. 2023 (cs-cha_magao2022 image), which was not recovered in that dataset.

paper.title: First direct detection of a polarized companion outside of a resolved circumbinary disk around CS Cha
